message.content:
When it comes to jazz vocalists, several names consistently rise to the top of critics’ lists and fan polls alike. While “best” is ultimately a matter of personal taste, here’s a quick rundown of the most celebrated jazz singers—along with a brief note on why they’re so revered:

| Singer | Why They’re Iconic |
|--------|--------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and effortless phrasing set a gold standard for jazz vocals. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her deeply emotive delivery and unique phrasing turned standards into personal statements; she remains a touchstone for lyrical depth. |
| **Sarah Sullivan** | A powerhouse of range and control, Sullivan’s blend of blues, gospel, and jazz made her a standout in the 1950s and ’60s. |
| **Louis Armstrong** | Though famed as a trumpeter, his gravelly voice and charismatic stage presence made him one of the first true crossover stars. |
| **Nat King Cole** | His smooth baritone and sophisticated phrasing earned him the nickname “The King of Swing.” |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | A modern torch singer whose soulful voice and contemporary approach keep the tradition alive. |
| **Diana Krall** | A pianist‑vocalist hybrid who blends jazz standards with a cool, intimate style. |
| **John Coltrane** (as a vocalist) | Though primarily a saxophonist, his vocal work on *A Love Supreme* shows his deep spiritual connection to music. |

These artists have shaped the sound of jazz singing across decades, each bringing a distinct voice and emotional depth that continues to inspire musicians and listeners alike.
